_about: A18 line clauses. Each entry names what one lesson must say on screen about what its engine leaves out. Source: docs/conformance-matrix.md (PR #148). 'require' patterns must all match the text of ONE tour step, and that step must carry a claim whose source matches 'source'. 'banInLine' applies to that step. 'banAnywhere' applies to the whole tour, claims included. 'example' is a line that passes, for the self-check. The words of the real line belong to the tour author. 'alsoPasses' holds more lines that pass, written in the standard's own names, for the self-check. 'readClaims' adds the text of the step's own claims to the line, for a line that lives in a claim. Limit: 'absent' is one word anywhere on the step, so a step that says 'This engine runs P-256' with 'not' elsewhere passes this clause. The A18.refuse clauses and the A15a reader catch that line. A name with an underscore beside it is a whole name, so the patterns use (?<![a-z]) and (?![a-z]) in place of a word boundary.

lines.example: This engine leaves out HelloRetryRequest, P-256, RSA and ECDSA signatures, and ChaCha20.
alsoPasses: It leaves out HelloRetryRequest, the secp256r1 group, rsa_pkcs1_sha256, rsa_pss_rsae_sha256, ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256, and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.

lines.example: This engine leaves out the 3DES suite, session resumption, and the client certificate.
alsoPasses: It leaves out TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA, the suite RFC 4346 requires, session resumption, and the client certificate.

lines.example: The RSA class says false on bad padding. It does not stay quiet, so the TLS 1.1 server hides the answer. Do not copy this class.
This engine leaves out rekey, password login, 3des-cbc, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 and ssh-dss.
alsoPasses: It leaves out re-keying, password login, 3des-cbc, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 and ssh-dss.

lines.example: This check leaves out revocation, policy processing, and name constraints.
This lab does not run every DPoP step. It runs only some of them, with EdDSA only, and the caller stops a replay.
This lesson runs AES DUKPT, from ANSI X9.24-3.
If a reader's registers leak, past keys stay safe and later keys do not. A single leaked PIN key exposes only that sale.
